A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M2S study. The complete 13-page v1 and 19-page v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and the appendix report original jailbreak evaluations across four LLMs and Llama Guard, including attack success, harmfulness, adoption frequencies, and tactic analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds CoSafe and ATTACK_600 evaluations, token-count measurements, and a paired usage example.

M1.justification: The Hyphenize, Numberize, and Pythonize conversions and per-conversation best-of-three ensemble remain unchanged. Minor delimiter and code-formatting edits in Section 3 do not establish a different conversion procedure.

E1.justification: Appendices A–C extend actual evaluation beyond MHJ to ATTACK_600's lengthy instruction conversations and CoSafe's succinct scenario-driven adversarial queries. This broadens the represented conversation styles; JailbreakBench threshold calibration was already present in v1.

E2.justification: The original multi-turn conversations remain the comparator, alongside the same three M2S variants and ensemble. The added benchmarks reuse this comparison structure; no additional attack baseline is evaluated.

E3.justification: New Section 4.4 introduces token-count evaluation using tiktoken's o200k_base encoding, comparing conversation history through the final request with consolidated M2S input. The original model set, StrongREJECT judge, 0.25 ASR threshold, and best-of-three evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused token-efficiency analysis across three datasets and a paired multi-turn/M2S screenshot example in Appendix E. The 'Extended Tactic-Level Analysis' retains the original tactic groups and numerical evidence, adding explanations rather than new ablations.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports token-count standard deviations of 728.9 and 340.2 for multi-turn and M2S inputs. These describe token-length dispersion, not repeated-run uncertainty. Both versions still state that a single experiment was conducted per model, without confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in original Tables 1–6 are retained, with the tactic tables becoming Tables 8–10. New Tables 6–7 report CoSafe and ATTACK_600 outcomes, including GPT-4o ensemble ASRs of 67.0% and 91.0%, respectively. Tables 4–5 add token measurements, including MHJ averages of 2732.24 versus 1096.36 tokens.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same mathematical description of sequential dialogue and consolidated single-turn inference. No substantive formal definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The first-systematic-conversion, attack-effectiveness, and safeguard-bypass claims retain their meaning. The revised abstract adds the specific claim that average token usage falls by more than half, sharpening the previously qualitative efficiency claim.

C2.justification: Section 7 expands two implementation-focused limitations into substantial qualifications concerning curated datasets, attainable versus best-case performance, judge and threshold reliability, black-box mechanisms, deployment costs, and absent defenses. Appendix D also adds mechanism explanations for why particular tactics survive or weaken after consolidation.

D1.justification: v1 provides an anonymous dataset link. v2 reports a public release of code, conversion prompts, model responses, scores, and token fields across three datasets, describing 22,992 prompt records in Section 5.6. It also specifies the token-counting library and encoding. These are expanded disclosures; external resource availability was not verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds the benchmark-related works by Ren et al. on Derail Yourself and Yu et al. on CoSafe. The central research positioning remains unchanged. Numerous other references receive publication metadata updates, including Crescendo and GPTFuzzer/LLM-Fuzzer, rather than representing different cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract is substantially rewritten, the limitations become an extensive numbered discussion, and the formerly table-only appendix is reorganized into six named sections with explanatory prose. Dedicated data-availability and ethical-considerations sections further restructure the document, while much of the original methodology and results narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, four tables are added, and Appendices E–F introduce two screenshots and eight plots, including visualizations of retained results. Some new displays mislead: Figure 9's caption incorrectly says Mistral favors Pythonize, while Figures 10–11 label inherited tactic scores above 1 as differences on the 0–1 StrongREJECT scale.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's MHJ-centered evidence and qualitative efficiency argument, v2 provides broader benchmark support, documented token measurements, clearer resource disclosures, and more candid limitations. These improve support and transparency. However, the new Figure 9 interpretation contradicts Table 3, and Figures 10–11 introduce misleading metric labels. These reporting errors limit the net quality gain.
